## Objective
- Update the existing lightsaber-building game with a collection feature that lets players keep, name, view, and auction completed sabers.

## Requirements
- After pressing Finish, offer the choice to keep the lightsaber and add it to a collection.
- Allow players to name a saber or generate a random name.
- Add a Collection button under the “sybersmith” area, next to “Build a Legacy”; add an Activities button beside it for future work.
- Create an attractive collection display room with a central podium, hovering lightsaber, saber name, and a collapsible Parts list.
- Provide left/right arrows to browse multiple collected sabers.
- Make collected sabers available to sell at auction.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions have been made.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the project root and found `game.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `auction.css`.

### Active
- None; implementation has not started.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the game’s existing UI, build/finish flow, collection or auction systems, and persistence in `index.html`, `game.js`, `styles.css`, and related files.
2. Implement the finish prompt, saber naming/random naming, collection navigation and display, Parts disclosure, and auction listing integration.
3. Run the game and verify the flows visually and functionally.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Main game interface.
- `game.js`: Game behavior and likely builder/auction logic.
- `styles.css`: Main game styling.
- `auction.css`: Auction styling.

## Important Context
- The user asked for a complete, playable update and asked not to be asked clarifying questions.
- No files have been changed and no tests or screenshots have been run.

## Objective
- Update the existing lightsaber-building game so players can keep, name, view, and auction completed sabers.

## Requirements
- After pressing Finish, offer the choice to keep the lightsaber and add it to a collection.
- Let players name a saber or generate a random name.
- Add Collection and Activities buttons under the “sybersmith” area, next to “Build a Legacy”; Activities is for future work.
- Create an attractive collection room with a central podium, hovering lightsaber, saber name, and a collapsible Parts list.
- Add left/right navigation arrows when the collection has multiple sabers.
- Make collected sabers available to sell at auction.
- Complete the update without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions have been made.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected `index.html`, `game.js`, `styles.css`, and `auction.css`; identified the main interface, game logic, and auction styling.

### Active
- None; implementation has not started.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the remaining builder finish flow, auction integration, and persistence in `game.js` and related files.
2. Implement the collection choice, naming, collection display/navigation, Parts disclosure, and auction listing integration.
3. Run the game and verify the flows visually and functionally.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Main game interface.
- `game.js`: Game behavior, builder flow, and likely auction logic.
- `styles.css`: Main game styling.
- `auction.css`: Auction styling.

## Important Context
- No files have been changed; no tests or screenshots have been run.

## Objective
- Update the existing lightsaber-building game so players can keep, name, view, and auction completed sabers.

## Requirements
- After pressing Finish, offer the choice to keep the lightsaber and add it to a collection.
- Let players name a saber or generate a random name.
- Add Collection and Activities buttons under the “sybersmith” area, next to “Build a Legacy”; Activities is for future work.
- Create an attractive collection room with a central podium, hovering lightsaber, saber name, and a collapsible Parts list.
- Add left/right navigation arrows when the collection has multiple sabers.
- Make collected sabers available to sell at auction.
- Complete the update without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Added Collection and Activities navigation buttons to the workbench rail; collection count will be shown on the Collection button.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected `index.html`, `game.js`, `styles.css`, and `auction.css`, including finish flow, auction integration, and saber rendering.
- Added Collection and Activities navigation buttons with a collection count placeholder to `index.html`.

### Active
- Implementing the keep/name/random-name flow, collection persistence and room, navigation, Parts disclosure, and auction access.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add the collection display and keep/name prompt to `index.html`.
2. Implement collection persistence, random naming, collection navigation and parts disclosure in `game.js`.
3. Connect saved saber builds to the existing auction flow.
4. Style the new navigation and collection view, then verify the complete flow.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Workbench markup, navigation, auction overlay; includes the new Collection and Activities buttons.
- `game.js`: Builder state, finish/auction flow, Three.js saber model and collection behavior to add.
- `styles.css`: Main workbench and responsive styling.
- `auction.css`: Existing auction room styles.

## Important Context
- Current finish button invokes `nextStep()`; the final step calls `openSale()`.
- `selected` stores option indexes for each saber component; `rebuildSaber()` constructs the 3D model and `syncAuctionSaber()` clones it for auction.
- No tests or visual verification have been run.

## Objective
- Update the existing lightsaber-building game so players can keep, name, view, and auction completed sabers.

## Requirements
- After pressing Finish, offer the choice to keep the lightsaber and add it to a collection.
- Let players name a saber or generate a random name.
- Add Collection and Activities buttons under “sybersmith,” next to “Build a Legacy”; Activities is for future work.
- Create an attractive collection room with a central podium, hovering lightsaber, saber name, and a collapsible Parts list.
- Add left/right navigation arrows when the collection has multiple sabers.
- Make collected sabers available to sell at auction.
- Complete the update without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Collection and Activities navigation buttons are on the workbench rail; Collection has a count placeholder.
- Added a keep/name prompt with “Keep in collection” and “Skip to auction” choices, plus a dedicated collection-room overlay in `index.html`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Collection and Activities navigation buttons to `index.html`.
- Added keep/name dialog and collection-room markup to `index.html`.

### Active
- Implement collection persistence, random naming, collection navigation and Parts disclosure in `game.js`.
- Connect saved saber builds to auction access.
- Style navigation, keep prompt, and collection room; verify the full flow.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the keep/name dialog and name generation in `game.js`; make Finish open it before auction.
2. Persist named builds and selected component indexes in local storage, then render the collection room, navigation, Parts list, and auction action.
3. Add styles for the new navigation and overlays in `styles.css`.
4. Verify the complete build → keep → collection → auction flow.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Contains navigation, keep/name prompt, collection-room and existing auction markup.
- `game.js`: Builder state, 3D saber construction, auction flow, and upcoming collection behavior.
- `styles.css`: Workbench styling and location for navigation and collection styles.
- `auction.css`: Existing auction room styles.

## Important Context
- Final build step currently calls `openSale()` through `nextStep()`.
- `selected` stores component option indexes; `rebuildSaber()` constructs the 3D model and `syncAuctionSaber()` clones it for auction.
- Collection-room HTML includes `collectionSaber` canvas, `collectionPrev`, `collectionNext`, `collectionParts`, and `auctionCollected` controls.
- No tests or visual verification have been run.

- Update the lightsaber-building game so players can name and keep completed sabers in a collection, view them in an attractive collection room, and send collected builds to auction.

- Persist collection and make saved sabers available for auction.
- Complete the update without asking clarifying questions.

- Collection and Activities buttons are on the workbench rail; Collection shows a count.
- Added a keep/name prompt and collection-room overlay in `index.html`.

- Collection visuals and responsive styles are in a new `collection.css`.

- Added Collection and Activities navigation, keep/name prompt, and collection-room markup in `index.html`.

- Auctioning a collected saber loads its saved components and uses the artifact name for the auction lot.
- No tests or visual verification have been run.

## Objective
- Complete the lightsaber-building game update so players can name and keep sabers, browse their collection, and send saved builds to auction.

## Requirements
- After finishing, offer “Keep in collection” or “Skip to auction.”
- Support custom or randomly generated saber names.
- Add Collection and Activities navigation alongside “Build a Legacy”; Activities is for future work.
- Provide a collection room with a central podium, hovering saber, saber name, collapsible Parts list, and navigation arrows.
- Persist the collection and make saved builds available for auction.
- Complete the update without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Collection and Activities buttons are on the workbench rail; Collection shows a count.
- Collection is stored in local storage under `sabersmith.collection.v1`.
- Auctioning a collected saber loads its saved components and uses its name for the auction lot.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Collection and Activities navigation, keep/name prompt, collection-room markup, random naming, local persistence, collection browsing, Parts disclosure, and auction access for saved builds.
- Added a dedicated Three.js collection display and responsive styling.
- Changed the final build action to “FINISH SABER” and wired it to the keep/name prompt.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` completed without errors.

### Active
- Verify the full build → keep → collection → auction flow and address bugs or visual issues.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the app and test finishing a saber, keeping it with a custom/random name, reloading to confirm persistence, browsing multiple sabers, and auctioning a collected saber.
2. Check responsive collection-room layout, podium/model rendering, and auction lot naming.
3. Review changes and run available checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Navigation, keep/name dialog, collection-room and auction markup.
- `game.js`: Builder state, local collection storage, collection rendering/navigation, and auction flow.
- `collection.css`: Navigation and responsive keep-prompt/collection-room styling.
- `styles.css`: Existing base styles and layout.
- `auction.css`: Existing auction-room styles.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: `game.js` and `index.html` modified; `collection.css` added.
- No end-to-end or visual verification has been run.
